note_claims.claim: Panic attacks for 4 months.
Recurrent panic attacks with palpitations, breathlessness, hand tingling and fear of dying.
Panic attacks lasting about 10 minutes.
Frequency: two to three times a week now and increasing.
Symptoms: Anticipatory anxiety and generalised worry.
Sleep: satisfactory.
Mood: 'fed up' but not depressed.
Safety: No thoughts of self-harm or suicide.
Caffeine: about four coffees a day.
Alcohol: a couple of glasses of wine at weekends.
Drug use: No.
Work status: Currently off work with stress.
Thyroid: function normal last month.
Medications and allergies: No regular medications. No known drug allergies.
GAD-7 score: 15.
PHQ-9 score: 8.
Panic disorder with agoraphobic avoidance and generalised anxiety symptoms.
No risk to self identified.
Self-referral details for NHS Talking Therapies (CBT).
Start sertraline 25 mg once daily for 1 week, then 50 mg once daily.
Warned of possible initial increase in anxiety (due to sertraline).
Review in 3 months.
Reduce caffeine gradually.
If thoughts of self-harm, call NHS 111 (mental health option) or Samaritans 116 123.

transcript_facts.fact: Patient reports having panic attacks with palpitations, breathlessness, hand tingling, and fear of dying.
Panic attacks have been occurring for about four months, since around the start of summer.
Frequency of attacks is two or three times a week now, and they are getting worse.
Each panic attack lasts about ten minutes, but the patient feels wiped out afterward.
Patient avoids supermarkets and will not get on the Underground.
Patient worries about everything else, including work and money.
Patient reports sleep is okay and they get off to sleep fine.
Patient's mood is 'a bit fed up' but not depressed.
Patient reports no thoughts of harming themselves or ending their life.
Patient consumes about four coffees a day, or six if counting those at work.
Patient consumes a couple of glasses of wine at the weekend.
Patient reports no drug use.
Patient works in marketing and has not had any time off.
Relative is off at the moment with stress, and work has been awful for both of them.
Patient denies problems with heart or thyroid, and the thyroid was normal last month.
Patient reports no allergies.
Questionnaire scores are GAD-7 is 15 and PHQ-9 is 8, fitting with significant anxiety and panic disorder rather than depression.
Treatment with the best evidence for panic disorder is talking therapy called CBT.
Clinician suggests trying an SSRI called sertraline alongside therapy.
Medication plan: Start low at 25 milligrams once a day for a week, then increase to 50 milligrams once a day.
Clinician plans to see the patient in two weeks for a review.
Safety-netting: If thoughts of self-harm occur, call 111 (mental health option) or Samaritans on 116 123.
